# Data Provenance & Assumptions

**All data in this repository is synthetic**, generated by `scripts/generate_data.py`
(seed 42, fully reproducible). No real company or customer data is used.

Lumora is a fictional European B2B workflow-analytics SaaS (2023-01 → 2025-12),
selling per-seat subscriptions on four plans to SMB, Mid-Market and Enterprise accounts.

## Encoded behaviours (what a model or analysis *should* be able to find)

| Behaviour | How it is generated |
|---|---|
| Growth | New logos ~55/month growing ~2.8% monthly, with July/August/December slowdowns |
| Segment mix | SMB 62% / Mid-Market 30% / Enterprise 8% overall, varying by channel |
| Churn | Monthly base hazard SMB 3.4%, MM 1.6%, ENT 0.7%; higher in first 3 months; annual contracts churn only at renewal |
| Churn driver | A hidden per-customer engagement score drives both seat utilisation/usage **and** churn — so usage data contains genuine predictive signal |
| Channel quality | Organic and Partner customers are more engaged; Paid Social customers are less engaged (cheap to acquire ≠ valuable) |
| Expansion | Highly utilised, engaged accounts add seats or upgrade plans |
| Collections | ~2% payment failure, higher for disengaged customers |
| CAC | Cost-per-logo targets by channel (Organic ~€1k … Outbound ~€7.5k) with noise |

## Known limitations
- No reactivations, trials, discounts beyond annual pre-pay, multi-currency or tax.
- One sales rep per customer; no opportunity/pipeline data (a Salesforce-style extension is a possible follow-up).
- Behaviour is stylised: useful to demonstrate method, not to benchmark real SaaS performance.
